channel.title: Knowledge Center
channel.description: New and updated Insights, Playbooks, Frameworks, Templates, Case Studies, and more.

item.title: Delivery controls that earn their place
item.description: Most delivery controls are monitoring with a governance label. A control earns its place only if it can change what leadership decides.

item.title: The requirements decision hierarchy
item.description: Which requirements need a full decision record, which need traced rationale, and which need neither. A screen based on consequence and reversal.

item.title: Delivery Control Assessment Template
item.description: A one-page sheet for running the Control Sufficiency Test across a control portfolio, recording the verdict and the action for each control.

item.title: Requirements Decision Review Checklist
item.description: A decision record that cannot survive review is not governance. Verify statement, rationale, alternatives, ownership, and revisit trigger before accepting one.

item.title: Adoption Is the Real Go-Live
item.description: Cutover is a technical event; adoption is the business one. The Adoption Ledger tracks the behaviors that prove a transformation actually landed.

item.title: Assurance Is What Lets Leaders Say Yes
item.description: Governance that only says no is cost. Proportionate Assurance scales scrutiny to consequence, so leaders approve fast with evidence behind them.

item.title: Automate the Toil, Not the Judgment
item.description: Automation fails when it creeps into decisions that need judgment. The Toil-Judgment Line shows what to automate, what to assist, and what to keep human.

item.title: Requirements Are Decisions, Not Documents
item.description: Requirements fail after sign-off because a document records what was agreed, not why. The RDR Model reframes them as durable decision records that cut rework.

item.title: The Platform Decision That Constrains the Next Decade
item.description: A platform choice is the adoption of a constraint set, not a purchase. The Constraint Horizon evaluates five constraint classes before any demo.

item.title: The Status Report That Tells the Truth
item.description: Status theater hides trouble until recovery is expensive. The Evidence-Backed Status model pairs every claim with evidence, trend, and a decision.

item.title: Enterprise AI & Automation Strategy Playbook
item.description: A practical methodology for identifying, prioritizing, designing, governing, and measuring AI and automation initiatives across business operations.

item.title: Enterprise Data Governance Playbook
item.description: A complete methodology for governing data quality, ownership, lifecycle, master data, and compliance, and for building AI-ready data foundations.

item.title: Enterprise Discovery Playbook
item.description: A consultant-grade approach to enterprise discovery across processes, systems, stakeholders, and risks, so solution design starts from evidence.

item.title: Enterprise Integration Strategy Playbook
item.description: A practical methodology for selecting, designing, governing, and evolving enterprise integrations across ERP, CRM, AI automation, and legacy systems.

item.title: Enterprise Project Delivery Playbook
item.description: A complete methodology for planning, governing, delivering, and improving enterprise transformation across Agile, Waterfall, and hybrid delivery models.

item.title: Enterprise Requirements Management Playbook
item.description: A complete methodology for managing requirements from discovery to implementation, with the RDR Model at its center and traceability that survives delivery.

item.title: Enterprise Solution Design Playbook
item.description: A structured approach to turning a requirements baseline into implementable solution architecture, with decisions recorded and constraints faced early.

item.title: The Stakeholder Power-and-Posture Map
item.description: Power without support sinks programs. The Power-and-Posture Map diagnoses six stakeholder stances and prescribes the move each one needs.

item.title: Requirements Decision Record Template
item.description: A one-page, fillable record for capturing the decisions behind your requirements: the decision, its rationale, owner, assumptions, and revisit trigger.

item.title: Audit-Readiness Checklist
item.description: Audit-readiness should be a byproduct, not a project. Verify decisions, assurance tiers, evidence, lifecycle, and access before someone asks.

item.title: Auto-Generate a Status Digest from Your Tracker
item.description: Status assembly is toil. Automate the digest, keep the judgment, and design the seam that stands the automation down when tracker data goes stale.

item.title: The ERP and CRM Platform Landscape
item.description: Platform categories compared by the constraints they impose rather than the features they demo, an orientation map for ERP and CRM decisions.
